title: Delete Deprecated Command Shim Classes from Source Files
description: Delete all 16 deprecated command shim class bodies from 6 command source files. These classes are now dead code — Story 37 removed their Program.cs registrations. Files affected: AccountCommands.cs (1 class), ApiCommands.cs (1 class + section comment), ApiRegistryCommands.cs (5 classes + section comment), UtilCommands.cs (2 classes), ScopeCommands.cs (2 classes + section comment), TraceCommands.cs (6 classes + section comment). This is Phase 2 of the remove-deprecated-commands-1 plan.
prerequisiteState: Story 37 is complete. Program.cs has no references to any deprecated command class. All shim classes exist as unreferenced dead code.
goal: After this story: all deprecated shim class definitions are removed from the codebase. dotnet build succeeds with 0 errors. No file in src/ contains any deprecated command class body.
scope: In src/ZapiCli/Commands/AccountCommands.cs: locate and delete the AccountReAuthDeprecatedCommand class and its XML summary comment ('/// <summary>[Deprecated] Use account refresh instead.</summary>'). The class starts after the closing brace of AccountRefreshCommand, around line 226.

In src/ZapiCli/Commands/ApiCommands.cs: delete the '// ─── api call (deprecated alias for api request)' section comment and the entire ApiCallCommand sealed class body (including XML doc comment above it). The canonical ApiRequestCommand must not be touched.

In src/ZapiCli/Commands/ApiRegistryCommands.cs: delete the '// ─── deprecated shims for api registry *' section comment and all 5 deprecated shim classes: ApiRegistryListCommand, ApiRegistryAddCommand, ApiRegistryUpdateCommand, ApiRegistryShowCommand, ApiRegistryRemoveCommand. Each is a sealed class implementing AsyncCommand<ApiEndpoint*Settings>. The canonical ApiEndpoint*Command classes earlier in the file must not be touched.

In src/ZapiCli/Commands/UtilCommands.cs: delete the UtilTimeMsDeprecatedCommand sealed class (with its XML summary) and the UtilTimeNowDeprecatedCommand sealed class (with its XML summary). The canonical UtilTimestampCommand and UtilNowCommand must not be touched.

In src/ZapiCli/Commands/ScopeCommands.cs: delete the '// ─── deprecated shims (top-level scope kept for backward compatibility)' section comment and both ScopeAddDeprecatedCommand and ScopeListDeprecatedCommand sealed classes. The canonical ScopeAddCommand and ScopeListCommand must not be touched.

In src/ZapiCli/Commands/TraceCommands.cs: delete the '// ─── Deprecated trace session * shims' section comment and all 6 deprecated shim classes: DeprecatedSessionStartCommand, DeprecatedSessionListCommand, DeprecatedSessionExportCommand, DeprecatedSessionCloseCommand, DeprecatedSessionReopenCommand, DeprecatedSessionRemoveCommand. Each is sealed and calls DeprecationHelper.Warn(...) before delegating. The canonical trace commands (StartSessionCommand, ListSessionsCommand, etc.) must not be touched.
After all deletions, run 'dotnet build src/zapi-cli.sln' and verify 0 errors.
acceptanceCriteria: ApiRegistryCommands.cs contains no ApiRegistryListCommand, ApiRegistryAddCommand, ApiRegistryUpdateCommand, ApiRegistryShowCommand, or ApiRegistryRemoveCommand classes
UtilCommands.cs contains no UtilTimeMsDeprecatedCommand or UtilTimeNowDeprecatedCommand classes
ScopeCommands.cs contains no ScopeAddDeprecatedCommand or ScopeListDeprecatedCommand classes

TraceCommands.cs contains no DeprecatedSessionStartCommand, DeprecatedSessionListCommand, DeprecatedSessionExportCommand, DeprecatedSessionCloseCommand, DeprecatedSessionReopenCommand, or DeprecatedSessionRemoveCommand classes
All '// ─── deprecated shims' and '// ─── Deprecated...' section comments are removed
All canonical command classes (ApiEndpoint*Command, ScopeAddCommand, ScopeListCommand, StartSessionCommand, etc.) remain intact
dotnet build src/zapi-cli.sln exits 0 with no errors
contextForAgent: Each deprecated shim class follows an identical pattern: constructor takes the same service dependencies as the canonical command, ExecuteAsync calls DeprecationHelper.Warn(...) then delegates to the canonical command's logic (or re-instantiates the service call). They are all at the bottom of their respective files after a '// ─── deprecated shims' section divider comment. The canonical classes are at the top of the same files — never touch those. After this story, DeprecationHelper.Warn() will have zero callers; DeprecationHelper itself is deleted in Story 39.
